name: templr
description: Website design inspiration from a library of 106 templates and 19 demos across restaurants, cafes, shops, fashion, hotels, fitness, galleries, agencies, SaaS and local services. Search by business type, inspect real image previews, then download selected HTML and run it on your own computer with Hive Local. Includes template metadata and source files.
guidance: For website or landing-page ideas, inspiration, designs or previews, first search_templates with the business type. Present 3-5 real candidates with get_preview image blocks before generating new mockups. For clickable previews call the user's local-preview preview_templates tool: it downloads HTML to that computer and serves loopback URLs. Never present VPS localhost gallery links or 8b.com demo links as user-local previews. After the user chooses, read AGENTS.md and DESIGN.md, then index.html. If the local helper is unavailable, show images and explain how to enable Hive Local; do not claim a local server was started.
session_hint: For website inspiration, search templr with the actual business type, show 3-5 real get_preview images, and let the user choose before coding. For clickable HTML previews use the user's local-preview connection, which downloads files to their computer and starts a loopback server; never claim VPS localhost links are user-local previews.

name: Context7
description: Current library, framework, SDK and API documentation and code examples. Resolve a library ID, then query its documentation before relying on remembered APIs. Connect your own Context7 key with Hive Local; upstream limits belong to your account.
guidance: For library/framework/SDK/API setup, usage, migration or version-specific questions, resolve-library-id first, then query-docs for the specific topic. Skip resolution only when an exact /org/project library ID is already provided. Keep queries focused and never put credentials or private source into documentation queries.
session_hint: Use Context7 for current library and SDK documentation instead of remembered APIs.

name: Tinyfish
description: Remote web browsing, research and browser automation using your own Tinyfish account. Discover the connected server's current tools and their schemas before use. Your upstream usage and charges stay with your Tinyfish key.
guidance: Use Tinyfish when a task requires remote browsing or web interaction and its actual advertised tools fit. Inspect the current input schema. Respect the user's instruction about browsers and approvals; never submit purchases, messages or other consequential actions without authorization. Do not assume a tool name or invent a browser result.
session_hint: Use Tinyfish when external research or remote browser interaction fits, respecting the user's preferred tools and browsers.

name: MarkItDown
description: Convert web pages, PDFs, Word, PowerPoint and Excel documents, HTML, CSV, JSON, XML, EPUB, ZIP archives and images to clean Markdown for reading, summarizing and extraction. Shared by Hive for public https URLs; with Hive Local it also converts files on your own computer.
guidance: To read, summarize, quote or extract data from a document or web page, call convert_to_markdown with uri set to an https:// URL, a data: URI, or (with Hive Local) a file:// path inside an approved folder. Work from the returned Markdown instead of fetching raw HTML. For PDFs and office files this keeps headings and tables. Combine with DuckDB for tables and with filesystem to save the result locally.
session_hint: Use markitdown to turn web pages and documents into Markdown before reading them.

name: DuckDB
description: Analytical SQL with DuckDB: query CSV, Parquet and JSON files by URL, profile and summarize datasets, join and aggregate. Shared by Hive for public https data with a sandbox that blocks server files and writes. With Hive Local it queries files in your approved folders and configured local DuckDB databases on your own computer.
guidance: For data questions over CSV, Parquet or JSON, call execute_query with DuckDB SQL such as SELECT * FROM read_csv_auto('https://...') LIMIT 20, DESCRIBE or SUMMARIZE. Results are capped; aggregate in SQL instead of pulling raw rows. Each shared query runs in a fresh session, so put the whole analysis in one statement (CTEs work). With Hive Local, enable duckdb with --database to choose an approved local DuckDB file; access defaults to read-only. Pass chart-ready aggregates to the next step.
session_hint: Use duckdb for SQL over CSV, Parquet or JSON data and for configured local databases.

prepare: import duckdb, os, sys; os.path.exists(sys.argv[1]) or duckdb.connect(sys.argv[1]).close()

import duckdb, gzip, os, urllib.request
platform = duckdb.connect().execute('PRAGMA platform').fetchone()[0]
version = 'v' + duckdb.__version__
target = os.path.expanduser('~/.duckdb/extensions/' + version + '/' + platform + '/httpfs.duckdb_extension')
if not os.path.exists(target):
    url = 'https://extensions.duckdb.org/' + version + '/' + platform + '/httpfs.duckdb_extension.gz'
    request = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={'User-Agent': 'hive-local/1'})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=60) as response:
        extension = gzip.decompress(response.read(33554432))
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(target), exist_ok=True)
    with open(target + '.tmp', 'wb') as output:
        output.write(extension)
    os.replace(target + '.tmp', target)

name: Filesystem
description: Read, search, write, edit and organize files and folders on your own computer through Hive Local. Access is limited to the folders you approve; nothing is uploaded except the results your agent asks for.
guidance: Call list_allowed_directories first; only those folders are reachable. Use search_files or directory_tree to locate files, read_text_file with head/tail for large files, and edit_file with dryRun before applying edits. write_file overwrites; confirm with the user before replacing existing files.

name: FFmpeg
description: Process video and audio files on your own computer through Hive Local: read media info, convert formats, compress, trim, merge clips, extract audio tracks, extract frames as images and burn in subtitles. Files stay on your machine inside approved folders.
guidance: Start with ffmpeg_get_info to read duration, codecs and resolution, then pick the operation. Outputs are written next to Hive Local's output folder unless output_path is given; report the output path to the user. Paths must be absolute and inside approved folders. Prefer ffmpeg_trim (stream copy) over re-encoding when only cutting.

name: Serena
description: Semantic code navigation and editing on your own computer through Hive Local, backed by language servers: symbol overviews, find symbols, references, implementations and declarations, diagnostics, and symbol-level edits, renames and safe deletes in your project.
guidance: Serena works on the project folder configured in Hive Local, with paths relative to it. Call initial_instructions once, then get_symbols_overview for a file and find_symbol with include_body for exact code. Use find_referencing_symbols before renaming or changing signatures, rename_symbol for refactors and get_diagnostics_for_file after edits. Prefer Hive's code_search for repositories indexed in Hive and Serena for live, uncommitted code.
